_comment: mock plugin, run against a coverage-instrumented esignet-service so the
report carries the per-surface coverage panel.
Same test selection as config.mock.json; the difference is where it points
and that run.coverage is on. Run the whole thing with compose, which builds
the instrumented server and brings up its dependencies and the suite:
docker compose -f coverage-docker-compose.yml up --build \
--abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from harness
'esignet' is the compose service name. That one spelling has to work from
three places at once -- the harness, the conformance suite, and the server's
own issuer claim -- because discovery has to be self-consistent or the suite
rejects it. Do not change it to localhost: the suite would then resolve it to
its own container.
The compose file sets two things this config cannot: ADMIN_TOKEN, because a
server started without ISSUER_URL and JWKS_URL installs no scope middleware
and never inspects the bearer (an explicit opt-in, so a real deployment
cannot go green on a broken IAM -- see api/steps.go); and CONFIG_LOCAL
pointing at overlay.none.json, because config.local.json normally aims
esignet.base_url at a deployed environment and is applied on top of this
file, which would drive that deployment while snapshotting the local
binary's counters.
The conformance surface additionally needs conformance-suite-private/*.json
to carry a discoveryUrl on http://esignet:8088 and clients registered on THIS
server -- the tracked copies point at a deployed environment. Without that,
select SURFACES=api,e2e.
run.coverage.dir is the harness's view of the snapshot directory and must
resolve to the same place as the server's GOCOVERDIR; compose does that with
a shared ./out mount.
